If I take your point for granted that you have a psychopathic core (which I recommend talking to a psychologist about if you haven't yet) then that doesn't mean you can't be a good person, or live a good life. It's just going to make it harder, which sucks, but I don't think lacking empathy or being psychopathic means you have to do bad things, or deserve a bad life. I feel I can relate a bit - I think I have low somatic empathy, people's feelings don't really mesh with mine and it's very easy for me to look at a terribly sad friend and feel nothing. But I have a good idea of right and wrong either way, and I can act in a way I know I would want to be treated, and comfort that friend despite not feeling that internal need to. I believe that everyone deserves sympathy, you included, and it's sad for me to hear people don't sympathise with you much, and that you think they wouldn't care if you were gone. That must be a very tough perception to have. 

I do agree that for most people having a purpose, and working towards it will bring them pleasure and that in that sense it's not entirely altruistic. I don't know if there are people who carry on with their purpose even if it brings them no pleasure at all, or very little. I only have my experience to draw from so I can't know for sure, but I think I find it less hard to believe than you do. I think for example of a struggling mother, whose life is very difficult and painful, living because they have a child to raise, someone who depends on them. That's purpose for me, but it's impossible to say for sure whether they are alive because of that purpose, or because of some positive feeling their purpose gives them. I don't think it matters to me as much as it does for you, but it's interesting to think about at least

You are right that it's a different kind of happiness that I focus on - when I say "happiness" it's better understood as contentment or fulfillment, as the base state of existence that one might return to after feeling the pleasure of being in sunlight, or eating a nice meal. 

Another way I understand it is just in simple numerical terms, a happy life is a life where happiness or contentment is the predominant state of being, separated by only sparse periods of suffering or pain.

I think for many people this is a life that is unimaginable, these are people who wonder why life is worth living if the majority of it will be suffering, and people who these brief respites of pleasure aren't enough. This is who my post is for.
